tasks.short: Study MEMS technology characteristics and processing

steps.what: Frame the experimental or virtual study of potential MEMS technology, choosing hypotheses, physical assumptions and response measures
Set up the study's specimen or virtual-case matrix in the experimental-design and simulation category of {OTHER}, using native parameter tables and unit checks
Conduct experimental or virtual studies of MEMS characteristics and processing principles, supervising the actual runs and capturing observed outcomes and failed cases
Analyze response plots and physical meaning, write conclusions and check the final study snapshot; reuse native plotting settings while preserving failed cases and uncertainty
Save the exact checked MEMS study snapshot in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native case tables and repeatable response plots in the experimental-design and simulation category of {OTHER}. Keep hypotheses, actual run supervision and physical interpretation human, then save only the completed checked study snapshot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated case and plot setup can be reconstructed for related studies.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parameter tables and plot settings can reuse structure without choosing the physical model.
tasks.still_hard: Microscale effects, boundary assumptions and failed specimens need scientific explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises a numerical trend that does not establish a physical processing principle.

ambition.what: No autonomous experiment or process acceptance.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated setup, unchanged scientific responsibility.

reach.learn: Relate measured properties to specimen history and uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Native experimental matrices and plot settings can reduce repeated setup without establishing scientific validity.

assumptions: Boundary is a research study and saved record, not production process validation in 16507. Actual experiment work is retained; solver runtime and outside specimen manufacture earn no saving.

The engineer produces hypothesis, specimen or case ID, geometry, material parameters, units and boundary assumptions in s1-s2. Actual result, unit, run status and provenance are captured in s3. Missing inputs require manual investigation; scheduled cases never count as completed results.
Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Final s4 checking follows completed plots and conclusions and binds exact cases and results; edits void the save gate.
unknowns: Which native case and plot templates already exist
research_questions: What repeated setup remains in actual related MEMS studies?

already_counted.description: Case review and final scientific analysis remain in s2 and s4.

incremental.description: Maintain case templates and verify plotting definitions after software changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final cases, results, plots and conclusions checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Case and plot setup saves 8.8 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 6.8 net. Existing templates or novel studies give zero benefit. Scientific work and saving retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define MEMS device geometry, materials, tolerances and feasible fabrication constraints from actual device and facility evidence
Devise MEMS production methods, choosing integrated-circuit fabrication, lithographic electroforming or micromachining sequences and resolving material and step interactions
Set up explicit layer, mask and dimensional process cases in the MEMS process-modelling category of {OTHER}, reusing validated native sequence and geometry structures
Evaluate fabrication feasibility and sensitivities, write the proposed method and check its final sequence, evidence and limitations
Save the exact checked proposed MEMS method in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native layer and sequence reuse in the MEMS process-modelling category of {OTHER}. The engineer devises the actual fabrication method and judges interactions and feasibility before saving its final proposed version; no recipe is released to production.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layer and dimensional setup can distract from fabrication-method decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native process structures can reuse explicit geometry and sequence fields.
tasks.still_hard: Etch behaviour, stress, contamination and material compatibility need process expertise.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer anticipates how one fabrication step changes the next.
tasks.altitude: Less model setup, unchanged process-method judgement.

reach.learn: Check whether a proposed sequence is feasible on actual equipment.

evidence.claim: Explicit layer and sequence structures can be reused in native process modelling without proving fabrication feasibility.

assumptions: Boundary is devising and recording a proposed method, excluding production execution and validation in 16507. This is not a second copy of the technology study in 16506.

The device owner supplies dimensions, materials and tolerance requirements; the facility supplies tool limits and qualified process data. The engineer checks and enters layer, thickness, mask, sequence and process conditions in s1-s3. Missing or novel interactions require manual investigation, not guessed defaults.
Native reuse first. Illustrative shares are unmeasured. Final s4 checking follows the completed method and binds its exact sequence and caveats; edits void the save gate.
unknowns: Whether native layer and sequence reuse already covers setup
research_questions: Which setup fields repeat while the actual method changes?

already_counted.description: Process-case review and final method assessment remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain qualified sequence definitions and tool-limit fields.

approvals.approved_version: Final proposed sequence and limitations checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated case setup saves 5 gross hours less 1.5 upkeep for 3.5 net. Existing native structures give zero gain. Method invention, feasibility and saving retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop specialized materials characterization procedures for relevant thermal, fatigue, notch, abrasion or hardness behaviour, specifying specimens, fixtures, conditioning, calibration and acceptance rationale
Run procedure-validation trials and capture actual specimen preparation, calibration, loading, failures and repeat measurements

Validate the procedure using repeatability and response plots in the materials-test analysis category of {OTHER}; interpret failures, write limits and check the completed procedure and validation record
Save the exact checked procedure-validation snapshot in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native repeatability and response plots in the materials-test analysis category of {OTHER}. Keep procedure design, actual trials and scientific validation human, with final procedure limits checked before the versioned save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated analysis-chart setup can accompany each procedure validation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native test-analysis settings can reuse arithmetic and plotting structure.
tasks.still_hard: Specimen effects and fixture artefacts can make a repeatable procedure invalid.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer distinguishes the material response from the test apparatus response.

ambition.what: No new procedure-release or accreditation authority.

tasks.altitude: Less plot setup, unchanged validation responsibility.

reach.learn: Trace uncertainty to actual preparation and calibration conditions.

evidence.claim: Repeatability and response plotting can use native settings while procedure validity requires scientific judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is development and validation of a characterisation procedure, not production process qualification or technician labour. The laboratory-test category of {OTHER} supports actual measurement capture in s2.

The engineer defines specimen ID, preparation, fixture, calibration, load or temperature sequence, unit and acceptance rationale in s1 and captures actual readings and deviations in s2. Missing readings or calibration evidence require manual resolution and retesting, counted in s2-s3.

Native plotting first; shares are illustrative and unmeasured. No test-runtime saving is claimed. The completed procedure and validation wording exist before the final s3 check; edits require rechecking before save.
unknowns: Which native validation plots already exist
research_questions: Does repeated chart setup materially interrupt procedure validation?

already_counted.description: Analysis, scientific interpretation and final procedure checks remain in s3.

incremental.description: Maintain plot settings and verify changed measurement exports.

approvals.approved_version: Final procedure, actual validation evidence and limits checked in s3; edits void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Plot setup saves 3.6 gross hours less 1 upkeep for 2.6 net. Already configured plots give zero gain. Procedure design, physical trials and scientific checking retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the fabrication-process validation scope, sampling, statistical assumptions and acceptance rules and verify actual lot, tool and measurement provenance
Conduct or supervise actual process-validation trials and life tests, capturing lot outcomes, failures and deviations
Validate MEMS fabrication processes using configured statistical process-control charts and stated process-simulation cases in the process-validation analysis category of {OTHER}
Interpret variation, model limits and life-test failures; write the validation finding and check the final record against actual process evidence without automatically accepting the process
Save the exact checked process-validation record in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native statistical charts and explicit simulation-case settings in the process-validation analysis category of {OTHER}. The engineer verifies actual lots, conducts trials, interprets variation and checks the completed record before saving; no chart automatically releases a fabrication process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated chart and case assembly can be manual despite structured process results.
tasks.enabler_now: Native statistical analysis can reuse explicit subgroup and calculation settings.
tasks.still_hard: Stable variation alone does not establish suitability, adequate life or causal control.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer identifies when a validation conclusion exceeds the sampled process evidence.
tasks.altitude: Less statistical setup, unchanged process-validation responsibility.

reach.learn: Distinguish control limits from specification limits and acceptance rules.

evidence.claim: Configured statistical charts can reduce repeated calculations but do not establish process qualification by themselves.

assumptions: Boundary is validation of an identified fabrication-process version, separate from method design in 16499 and exploratory technology work in 16506. Actual physical trials and other-role work earn no saving.

Process records supply lot, tool, recipe version, timestamp, specimen, measurement, unit and calibration reference. The engineer verifies and captures subgroup definition, exclusions and actual trial outcomes in s1-s2. Missing provenance is investigated manually, not filled from a planned lot.

Native analysis first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Final s4 checking follows the completed charts and finding and binds exact dataset, process version and limitations; edits void the save approval.
unknowns: Whether sampling and life-test data support the intended conclusion
research_questions: Which repeated statistical assembly is still performed by the engineer?

already_counted.description: Statistical review and final scientific validation record remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain subgroup rules and revalidate changed process-data fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed validation dataset, process version and finding checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated statistical setup saves 12.5 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 10.5 net. Existing native analysis gives zero gain. Trials, provenance checks, interpretation and save retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated MEMS case and statistical setup can shrink while physical research and validation remain engineering work.
reach: Coordinate with fabrication, materials and quality specialists on actual process evidence.
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who makes each MEMS study and validation conclusion traceable to actual specimens, cases and process versions.
